item.title: Looking back at West Norfolk headlines from the archives
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Looking back at West Norfolk headlines from the archives
This week we look back at local news from late September 1961. Among the stories reported at the time, a 17-year-old farmworker from Sedgeford was fined one pound by Docking magistrates for cycling without due care and attention following a collision in Heacham.
Elsewhere in the region, Lynn Town Council discussed plans for a new cattle market and potential town expansion. Meanwhile, in 1986, comedian Norman Collier brought the cast of Hunstanton’s summer show to the King’s Lynn town hall for a reception with the Mayor. The theatre production had enjoyed a successful nine-week run at the Princess Theatre, prompting organisers to arrange free return coach travel for local theatre-goers.

item.title: Inquest concludes into death of retired King’s Lynn police officer
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Inquest concludes into death of retired King’s Lynn police officer
An inquest at Norfolk Coroner’s Court has ruled that 65-year-old Patrick Kavanagh died from a rare complication following a heart valve replacement. Mr Kavanagh, a retired police officer from Gaywood, was admitted to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in June last year suffering from chest pains and breathing difficulties. Despite receiving treatment, he suffered a cardiac arrest and passed away on July 1.
Area coroner Maeve Sykes concluded that the hospital provided appropriate care, noting that the death resulted from a rare mechanical valve dysfunction. The Queen Elizabeth Hospital trust has expressed its condolences to the family, confirming it had no concerns regarding the medical treatment provided to Mr Kavanagh.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/retired-police-officer-died-from-rare-complication-of-valv-9484303/

item.description:

North Lynn man to face court over building site burglaries
A 37-year-old man from North Lynn is due to appear at Norwich Crown Court next month to face charges related to building site burglaries in West Norfolk. Arunas Abartis, of Lady Jane Grey Road, has been charged with three counts of trespass and four counts of stealing diesel from sites in South Wootton, Hunstanton, Downham, and King’s Lynn.
The charges follow an arrest made by Norfolk Police on the evening of Monday, September 21. Mr Abartis has been bailed until his court appearance on October 21. Officers also conducted a search at a property on Lynn Road in Terrington St Clement earlier this week, though the police cordon at that location has now been removed.

New road markings installed at Gaywood clock junction
New cross-hatching has been painted at the Gaywood clock junction to help improve traffic flow. The markings are designed to prevent vehicles queuing from Wootton Road from blocking the junction, which previously restricted traffic travelling from Gayton Road.
Gaywood councillor Rob Colwell, who secured funding for the project through his Local Member Fund, said the change aims to ensure emergency service vehicles can pass through the area more easily. The work follows concerns raised by local residents and consultations with emergency services regarding congestion at the site. Councillor Colwell pursued the installation with Norfolk County Council following delays to road-lining schemes across the region.

Final week for West Norfolk development consultation
Residents in West Norfolk have until midnight on Monday, September 29, to share their views on the borough’s future Local Plan. The council is seeking public feedback on where new housing, schools, jobs, and transport links should be located.
While landowners have suggested various sites for potential development, the council confirms that no final selections have been made. Officials are particularly encouraging young people and those experiencing poverty to participate in the process. You can submit your comments online or collect a paper form from the reception at Kings Court on Chapel Street in King's Lynn. This consultation is an early step in the planning process, with a draft version of the plan expected to undergo further public review next year.

Wisbech students raise funds for hedgehog rescue
Three construction students from the College of West Anglia’s Wisbech campus have raised £294 for Ryston Rachel’s Hedgehog Hotel. Finn McAuley, Marc Watson and Erikas Rimkus created hedgehog houses using recycled materials, including old pallets and plastic bottles, as part of a WorldSkills project.
The initiative combined practical construction skills with a focus on sustainability and wildlife support. The rescue centre has reported high demand for the student-made houses, which have helped raise both funds and awareness for the local hedgehog population. College staff have praised the students for their teamwork and for applying their professional skills to benefit the community.

item.description:

New book explores the unusual history of King’s Lynn
A new book titled Quirky King’s Lynn has been released, detailing the town’s eccentric past. Author Bill Lovelock explores various legends, buildings, and characters, including tales of pirates, exorcists, and a mysterious fiddler. Mr. Lovelock, who previously wrote about Lowestoft, conducted his research by walking the streets of the town to uncover hidden details. The book highlights the town’s evolution from a major medieval port to a centre for industries like glassmaking and food canning. One notable feature is the story of the Wandering Piper, which links a local legend to the discovery of human and canine remains during road works in the 1930s. The book is now available for those interested in the area's history.
